Title: az_aks_nodepool_add(aks-preview)-3.yaml
Content: Syntax: az aks nodepool add [optional parameters]
- summary: Extra nodes used to speed upgrade. When specified, it represents the number or percent used, eg. 5 or 33%.
  name: --max-surge
- summary: The maximum number or percentage of nodes that can be simultaneously unavailable during upgrade. When specified, it represents the number or percent used, eg. 1 or 5%.
  name: --max-unavailable
- summary: Path to a file containing the desired message of the day. Only valid for linux nodes. Will be written to /etc/motd.
  name: --message-of-the-day
- summary: Minimun nodes count used for autoscaler, when "--enable-cluster-autoscaler" specified. Please specify the value in the range of [0, 1000] for user nodepool, and [1,1000] for system nodepool.
  name: --min-count
- defaultValue: User
  parameterValueGroup: Gateway, System, User
  summary: The mode for a node pool which defines a node pool's primary function. If set as "System", AKS prefers system pods scheduling to node pools with mode `System`. Learn more at https://aka.ms/aks/nodepool/mode.
  name: --mode
- defaultValue: "False"
  summary: Do not wait for the long-running operation to finish.
  name: --no-wait
- defaultValue: "3"
  summary: Number of nodes in the Kubernetes agent pool. After creating a cluster, you can change the size of its node pool with `az aks scale`.
  name: --node-count -c
- defaultValue: "0"
  summary: Size in GiB of the OS disk for each node in the agent pool. Minimum 30 GiB.
  name: --node-osdisk-size
- summary: OS disk type to be used for machines in a given agent pool. Defaults to 'Ephemeral' when possible in conjunction with VM size and OS disk size. May not be changed for this pool after creation. ('Ephemeral' or 'Managed').
  name: --node-osdisk-type
  parameterValueGroup: Ephemeral, Managed


Title: az_aks_create(aks-preview)-13.yaml
Content: Syntax: az aks create [optional parameters]
  parameterValueGroup: azure, cilium
- summary: The Kubernetes network plugin to use.
  description: Specify "azure" for routable pod IPs from VNET, "kubenet" for non-routable pod IPs with an overlay network, or "none" for no networking configured.
  name: --network-plugin
  parameterValueGroup: azure, kubenet, none
- summary: The network plugin mode to use.
  description: |-
    Used to control the mode the network plugin should operate in. For example, "overlay" used with
    --network-plugin=azure will use an overlay network (non-VNET IPs) for pods in the cluster.
  name: --network-plugin-mode
  parameterValueGroup: overlay
- summary: (PREVIEW) The Kubernetes network policy to use.
  description: |-
    Using together with "azure" network plugin.
    Specify "azure" for Azure network policy manager, "calico" for calico network policy controller, "cilium" for Azure CNI Overlay powered by Cilium.
    Defaults to "" (network policy disabled).
  name: --network-policy
- defaultValue: "False"
  summary: Do not use or create a local SSH key.
  description: To access nodes after creating a cluster with this option, use the Azure Portal.
  name: --no-ssh-key -x
- defaultValue: "False"
  summary: Do not wait for the long-running operation to finish.
  name: --no-wait
- defaultValue: "3"
  summary: Number of nodes in the Kubernetes node pool. It is required when --enable-cluster-autoscaler specified. After creating a cluster, you can change the size of its node pool with `az aks scale`.
  name: --node-count -c
- summary: The node initialization taints for node pools created with aks create operation.
  isPreview: true
  name: --node-init-taints --nodepool-initialization-taints


</Documents>
